parsed.summary: Tracing every sheet against the specification, the build matches the intended reference design: part numbers (STM32H753VITx/STM32F405RGTx, MIC26903YJL-TR, LD39200PU33R, INA219AIDCNR, PCA9685PW, W25N01GVZEIG_TR, 24CW1280T, BMI088/IIS2MDCTR/MPRLS0025PA00001A/TMP100, MAX-8Q, ABM8G-25MHz, TDD01H0SB1R, CH330), the stated values (R1=10mΩ, L1=15µH, R5/R6 giving Vout≈5V via 0.8·(1+R5/R6)), the power-rail topology (VCC→buck→+5V→LDO→+3.3V, no rail merging), the FCC↔NAVC UART2/I2C/GPIO links, and the verbatim schematic notes (including the documented MPRLS RESET/EOC swap bug) all agree with the spec. The only apparent mismatch — the PCA9685 note reading I2C 0x41 while the spec's table lists 0x40 — is not a board anomaly: the PCA9685 and INA219 share the I2C2_FCC bus, so 0x41 (A0 strapped high) is the conflict-free, intended value and the spec's table entry is simply a transcription error. The odd 31-pin buck symbol and the small I2C gate (U34) are present in the reference as well (the spec was written from this schematic) and do not change net behavior. No deviation that would make the board behave differently from the intended design is supported by the drawing.
